slides.title: Computational Catalysis and Emerging Materials Laboratory
slides.subtitle: Multiscale catalyst design integrating DFT, machine-learning potentials, and descriptors

slides.title: Why Study Catalysis Computationally

items: Reaction intermediates live for only **ps–ns**, so in-situ observation is hard — computation delivers *atomic-scale snapshots*
Active-site candidates explode to **10⁴–10⁶** combinations — purely experimental screening is too costly and slow
Trace activity and selectivity back to their *electronic-structure* origin, distilling them into **design principles**

body.text: → Computation accelerates *hypothesis generation* and *candidate selection*, letting experiments focus on validation — a **closed loop**.

slides.footer: Key idea: computation does not replace experiment — it *narrows the search space*

slides.title: A Multiscale Computational Stack

cards.head: DFT
cards.text: Adsorption energies, transition states, and the d-band center from *first principles*. The accuracy benchmark (ground truth), but it stalls at the *few-hundred-atom* scale.

cards.head: ML Potentials
cards.text: **MLIPs** (NequIP, MACE) trained on DFT give *DFT accuracy at MD speed* — extending to nanoparticles, dynamics, and ensemble sampling.

cards.head: Microkinetics
cards.text: Feed computed energies into **rate equations** to compare *turnover frequency*, the rate-determining step, and reaction orders directly with experiment.

slides.footer: A pipeline that *bridges scales* — from atoms to nanoparticles to reactor conditions

slides.title: Descriptors and Scaling Relations

body.text: Compressing complex activity into a few variables

items.head: Scaling relations
items.text: Adsorbate energies are *linearly* coupled, so a **single descriptor** (e.g. O binding energy) can predict activity.

items.head: Sabatier volcano
items.text: Bind too weakly and nothing activates; bind too strongly and the surface poisons — *an optimum exists*.

slides.footer: Next-generation design targets sites that *break scaling* — multimetallics and interfaces

slides.title: From ML Screening to Experiment

cards.head: ① Generate
cards.text: Combine compositions, facets, and defects into *tens of thousands* of candidate structures; pre-filter stability with an MLIP.

cards.head: ② Predict
cards.text: Regress activity and selectivity with descriptors and graph neural networks; *quantify uncertainty* to actively pick the next calculation (active learning).

cards.head: ③ Validate
cards.text: Synthesize and test only the top candidates, return the data, and retrain — a *closed loop* that accelerates discovery.

slides.footer: Case: alloy oxygen-reduction catalysts compressed from *10,000 candidates to ~10 experiments*
